problems.title: Pattern drill 1
problems.statement: Name the technique from the statement alone (60 seconds each).

parts.prompt: Find whether any two distinct elements of an unsorted array differ by exactly k.
Count subarrays whose sum is divisible by 7 (values may be negative).

hints: What does the brute force do over and over?
problems.solution: (a) Hash map / set: the brute force searches for x + k and x − k. (b) Prefix sums: the brute force recomputes range sums.

problems.title: Pattern drill 2
problems.statement: Name the technique from the statement alone (60 seconds each).

parts.prompt: In a sorted array, count pairs whose sum is at most T.
Longest substring containing at most 2 distinct characters.

hints: What does the brute force do over and over?
problems.solution: (a) Two pointers (sorted): the brute force checks all pairs although order tells you which side to discard. (b) Sliding window: the brute force re-examines windows that changed by one character.

problems.title: Pattern drill 3
problems.statement: Name the technique from the statement alone (60 seconds each).

parts.prompt: For each day's temperature, how many days until a warmer one?
Minimum ship capacity to deliver packages, in order, within D days.

hints: What does the brute force do over and over?
problems.solution: (a) Monotonic stack/deque: the brute force scans forward for the next larger element again and again. (b) Binary search on the answer: the brute force tries capacities one by one, though feasibility is monotone in capacity.

problems.title: Pattern drill 4
problems.statement: Name the technique from the statement alone (60 seconds each).

parts.prompt: Repeatedly merge the two smallest ropes; minimise total cost.
Number of ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps.

hints: What does the brute force do over and over?
problems.solution: (a) Heap: the brute force repeatedly finds the two smallest of a changing set. (b) Dynamic programming: the brute force recomputes the same subproblems.

problems.title: Pattern drill 5
problems.statement: Name the technique from the statement alone (60 seconds each).

parts.prompt: After each of 10⁵ friendship announcements, report whether persons a and b are connected.
Smallest element of a rotated sorted array.

hints: What does the brute force do over and over?
problems.solution: (a) Union-find / BFS: the brute force re-searches connectivity from scratch. (b) Binary search on the answer: the brute force scans although a monotone test (is the min to my right?) halves the range.

problems.title: Bottlenecks

parts.prompt: Brute force: for each i, for each j > i, sum a[i..j] in a loop. The first waste to remove?

hints: What is computed again and again?
problems.solution: Each range sum is recomputed from scratch; a running sum makes the inner loop O(1) per step, and prefix sums make any range O(1).

problems.title: Invariants
problems.statement: For the two-sum hash-map loop, which statement is the invariant at the start of iteration i?

options: seen contains every value in nums, with its index
seen contains every value at indices < i, with its index

hints: What's been inserted when iteration i begins?
problems.solution: Exactly the elements before i: that's why querying before inserting prevents an element from pairing with itself.

problems.title: Choosing tests
problems.statement: You've written a function returning the longest substring without repeating characters.

options: "abba" (the left edge must not move backwards)

hints: The example was already used to design the code.
problems.solution: Edge cases and adversarial structure find bugs; re-running the design example rarely does.

problems.title: Change the question
problems.statement: Count pairs (i, j) with i < j and a[i] > a[j] (inversions), n ≤ 10⁵.

parts.prompt: Which reframing gives O(n log n)?
options: For each j, count earlier elements greater than a[j], with a merge sort that counts while merging (or a Fenwick tree)

hints: Contribution per element instead of per pair.
problems.solution: Count each element's contribution: during merge sort, when an element of the right half is placed before remaining left-half elements, all of those form inversions with it. O(n log n). Changing the question from pairs to per-element contributions is the key move.

problems.title: Manual procedure as algorithm
problems.statement: You check by hand whether a word is a palindrome.

parts.prompt: What does your hand procedure suggest?
options: Compare the outer characters, then move inward: two pointers

hints: Watch what you do on the example.
problems.solution: Your manual procedure is the two-pointer algorithm: move 2 of the method in action.
